meta.title: Directive 2013/48/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 October 2013 on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings, and on the right to have a third party informed upon deprivation of liberty and to communicate with third persons and with consular authorities while deprived of liberty

items.text: This Directive lays down minimum rules concerning the rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and of persons subject to proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (‘European arrest warrant proceedings’) to have access to a lawyer, to have a third party informed of the deprivation of liberty and to communicate with third persons and with consular authorities while deprived of liberty.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings from the time when they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence, and irrespective of whether they are deprived of liberty. It applies until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person charged with a punishable act may exercise the right of defence, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is notified, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted.
The right of defense shall be exercised without more limitations than those expressly provided in this law from the attribution of the punishable act investigated until the extinction of the penalty

items.text: 2. This Directive applies to persons subject to European arrest warrant proceedings (requested persons) from the time of their arrest in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10.

provisions.comment: Spanish law recognizes the right of a lawyer to the one claimed by a European arrest warrant from the moment s/he is brought to justice and not from the moment of arrest
provisions.textEn: Once the detained person is brought to justice, s/he will be informed of the existence of the European arrest warran, of its contents, of his right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State whose function will be to assist the lawyer in Spain providing him/her with information and advice, of the possibility of consenting irrevocably his/her surrender to the issuing State in the hearing before the judge, as well as of the rest of his/her rights. In the event in which the appointment of a lawyer in the issuing State is requested, the issuing competent authority will be informed immediately

items.text: 3. This Directive also applies, under the same conditions as provided for in paragraph 1, to persons other than suspects or accused persons who, in the course of questioning by the police or by another law enforcement authority, become suspects or accused persons.

items.comment:
In Spain, penal sanctions for minor offences are always imposed by Courts having jurisdiction in criminal matters, so as this provision is not applicable. However, the Article 967.1 of the Criminal Procedural Law states that "In the summons forwarded to the complainant, the offended or injured person and the defendant to attend the trial for a minor crime, they will be informed that they might be assisted by a lawyer if they wish and that they must attend the trial with the means of evidence that they want to use. (...) Without prejudice to the provisions of the preceding paragraph, for the prosecution of minor crimes that carry the penalty of a fine whose maximum limit is at least six months, the general rules of defense and representation shall apply". This implies that cases of minor crimes, the assistance of a lawyer is optional, unless the crime carries a fine of more than six months.


In addition, in crimes against traffic safety, the detainee may renounce the right of attorney. In this sense, the Article 520.8 of the Criminal Procedural Law states that: "nevertheless, the detainee or prisoner may waive the mandatory assistance of a lawyer if his/her arrest is due to events which can be exclusively classified as crimes against traffic safety, provided that clear and sufficient information has been provided to the defendant in a simple and understandable language on the content of such right and the consequences of the waiver. The detainee may revoke his/her waiver at any time".

items.subHeading: The right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings

provisions.textEn:
Any person to whom a punishable act is attributed may exercise the right of defense, intervening in the proceedings, as soon as their existence is communicated, they have been arrested or any other precautionary measure or their processing has been agreed, for which purpose s/he will be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights:


d) Right to freely appoint a lawyer, without prejudice to the provisions of section 1 a) of article 527.


e) Right to request free legal aid, procedure to do it and conditions to obtain it.


To act in the procedure, people under investigation must be represented by a solicitor and defended by a lawyer, appointing them ex officio when the defendant had not made the appointment by him/herself and, in any case, when s/he had no legal aptitude to do so.

The detainee may freely appoint a lawyer and if s/he does not, s/he will be assisted by an ex officio lawyer. No authority or agent will make any recommendation on the lawyer to be appointed apart from informing him/her of his/her right.

The authority that holds the detained in custody shall immediately notify the Bar Association the name of the person designated by the detainee to assist him/her for the purposes of locating and transmitting the professional assignment or, where appropriate, communicating the request for the appointment of an ex officio lawyer.

If the detainee has not designated a lawyer, or the chosen one refuses the assignment or is not found, the Bar Association will immediately proceed to the appointment of an ex officio lawyer.

The designated lawyer will go to the detention center with the utmost speed, always within a maximum period of three hours from receipt of the order. If within that period it does not appear, the Bar Association will appoint a new ex officio lawyer who must appear as soon as possible and always within the indicated period, without prejudice to the disciplinary liability of the non-appearing lawyer.

items.text: Notwithstanding provisions of national law concerning the mandatory presence of a lawyer, Member States shall make the necessary arrangements to ensure that suspects or accused persons who are deprived of liberty are in a position to exercise effectively their right of access to a lawyer, unless they have waived that right in accordance with Article 9.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
In order to act in the process, people under investigation must be represented by a procurator and defended by a lawyer, being appointed ex officio when they have not been appointed by the defendant after being requested to do so, and in any case, when the investigated person does not have the legal capacity to do so.


If people under investigation have not appointed a procurator or lawyer, they shall be required to do so or those professionals shall be appointed ex officio if investigated persons do not comply with the requirement, when the case has reached the stage where their advice is needed or some remedy is to be attempted that makes their action indispensable.

The detainee may freely appoint a lawyer and if s/he does not, s/he will be assisted by an ex officio lawyer. No authority or agent will make any recommendation on the lawyer to be appointed apart from informing him/her of his/her right.

The authority that holds the detained in custody shall immediately notify the Bar Association the name of the person designated by the detainee to assist him/her for the purposes of locating and transmitting the professional assignment or, where appropriate, communicating the request for the appointment of an ex officio lawyer.

If the detainee has not designated a lawyer, or the chosen one refuses the assignment or is not found, the Bar Association will immediately proceed to the appointment of an ex officio lawyer.

The designated lawyer will go to the detention center with the utmost speed, always within a maximum period of three hours from receipt of the order. If within that period it does not appear, the Bar Association will appoint a new ex officio lawyer who must appear as soon as possible and always within the indicated period, without prejudice to the disciplinary liability of the non-appearing lawyer.

The investigating judge may give a reasoned decision on incommunicado detention or imprisonment when any of the following circumstances concur:

a) urgent need to avoid serious consequences that could endanger the life, freedom or physical integrity of a person, or

b) urgent need for immediate action by the investigating judge to avoid seriously compromising the criminal procedure.

In the cases of article 509, the detainee or prisoner may be deprived of the following rights if the circumstances of the case justify it:

a) Appoint his/her own lawyer

b) Communicate with all or any of the persons with whom s/he has the right to do so, except with the judicial authority, the Prosecutor and the Forensic Doctor

c) Meet privately with his/her lawyer.

d) Have access, personally or through his/her lawyer, to the proceedings, except to the essential elements to challenge the legality of the detention.

Member States shall respect the confidentiality of communication between suspects or accused persons and their lawyer in the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer provided for under this Directive. Such communication shall include meetings, correspondence, telephone conversations and other forms of communication permitted under national law.
items.heading: Article 4

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
All communications between the defendants and his lawyer will be confidential.

If these conversations or communications had been captured or intervened during the execution of any of the investigative proceedings regulated in this Law, the judge will order the elimination of the recording or delivery to the recipient of the detained correspondence, recording these circumstances in the minutes.

The provisions of the first paragraph shall not apply when the existence of objective evidence of the participation of the lawyer in the criminal act investigated or of its implication together with the defendant in the commission of another criminal offense is verified, without prejudice to the provisions of the General Penitentiary Law.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: The right to have a third person informed of the deprivation of liberty

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are deprived of liberty have the right to have at least one person, such as a relative or an employer, nominated by them, informed of their deprivation of liberty without undue delay if they so wish.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned will be informed in writing of their rights and especially the following (...) d) Right to be brought to the attention of the family member or person that the detainee wishes, without undue delay, his/her deprivation of liberty and place of custody where s/he stays

items.text: 2. If the suspect or accused person is a child, Member States shall ensure that the holder of parental responsibility of the child is informed as soon as possible of the deprivation of liberty and of the reasons pertaining thereto, unless it would be contrary to the best interests of the child, in which case another appropriate adult shall be informed. For the purposes of this paragraph, a person below the age of 18 years shall be considered to be a child.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
If the detainee is a minor, s/he will be made available to the Minors Sections of the Prosecutor's Office and the fact and place of custody will be communicated to those exercising parental responsability, guardianship or de facto custody thereof, as soon as there is proof of minority.

In case of conflict of interests with those who exercise parental rights, guardianship or de facto custody of the minor, a judicial defender will be appointed who will be informed of the fact and the place of detention.

If the detainee has his/her capacity judicially modified, the information provided for in section 2 of this article will be communicated to those who exercise the guardianship or de facto guardianship, reporting to the Prosecutor's Office.

If the detained, minor or with judicially modified capacity, were a foreigner, the fact of the arrest shall be notified ex officio to the Consul of his country

nationalActs.titleEn: Organic Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal responsibility of minors

provisions.textEn: Authorities and officials who intervene in the detention of a minor must manage it as harmlessly as possible and will be obliged to inform him/her, in a clear and understandable language and immediately, of the alleged facts, of the reasons of his/her detention and of his/her rights, especially those recognized in the Article 520 of the Criminal Procedure Law, as well as to guarantee their respect. They must also immediately notify the fact of the arrest and the place of custody to the minor's legal representatives and the Public Prosecutor's Office. If the minor detained is a foreigner, the fact of the arrest will be notified to the corresponding consular authorities if the minor has his/her habitual residence outside of Spain or when is requested by the minor himself or by his/her legal representatives.

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: The right to communicate, while deprived of liberty, with third persons

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are deprived of liberty have the right to communicate without undue delay with at least one third person, such as a relative, nominated by them.

This communication shall be held in the presence of a police officer or, where appropriate, of the official designated by the judge or prosecutor, without prejudice to the Article 527.

items.text: 2. Member States may limit or defer the exercise of the right referred to in paragraph 1 in view of imperative requirements or proportionate operational requirements.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: The right to communicate with consular authorities

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are non-nationals and who are deprived of liberty have the right to have the consular authorities of their State of nationality informed of the deprivation of liberty without undue delay and to communicate with those authorities, if they so wish. However, where suspects or accused persons have two or more nationalities, they may choose which consular authorities, if any, are to be informed of the deprivation of liberty and with whom they wish to communicate.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: If the detainee is a foreigner, the consul of his/her country will be informed of the fact of his/her detention and the place of custody and the detainee will be allowed to communicate with the consular authority. In the event that the detainee has two or more nationalities, s/he may choose which consular authorities should be informed of his/her deprivation of liberty and with whom s/he wishes to communicate.
If the detained, minor or person with judicially modified capacity, were a foreigner, the fact of the arrest shall be notified ex officio to the Consul of his/her country

items.text: 2. Suspects or accused persons also have the right to be visited by their consular authorities, the right to converse and correspond with them and the right to have legal representation arranged for by their consular authorities, subject to the agreement of those authorities and the wishes of the suspects or accused persons concerned.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: There is no reference to the right to have legal representation arranged for by their consular authorities
provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned will be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, as well as of his/her rights and especially the followings: (...) g) Right to be visited by the consular authorities of his/her country, to communicate and to mail with them.

items.text: 3. The exercise of the rights laid down in this Article may be regulated by national law or procedures, provided that such law or procedures enable full effect to be given to the purposes for which these rights are intended.

items.heading: Article 8
items.subHeading: General conditions for applying temporary derogations

items.text: 1. Any temporary derogation under Article 3(5) or (6) or under Article 5(3) shall

(a)

be proportionate and not go beyond what is necessary;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The incommunicado detention will last the time strictly necessary to urgently carry out diligence to avoid the dangers referred to in the previous section.

items.text:
(b)

be strictly limited in time;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
The incommunicado detention will last the time strictly necessary to urgently carry out diligence to avoid the dangers referred to in the previous section.

The incommunicado detention cannot be extended beyond five days. In cases where the prison responds to any of the crimes referred to in article 384 bis or other crimes committed in collusion and in an organized manner with two or more people, incommunicado detention may be extended for another period not exceeding five days.

items.text:
(c)

not be based exclusively on the type or the seriousness of the alleged offence; and

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The judicial order in which incommunicado detention is adopted or, where appropriate, its extension, must state the reasons why the measure has been adopted.

provisions.comment: The two reasons mentioned are of a taxative nature, without it being possible to adopt an incommicated detention if such circumstances do not concur.
provisions.textEn:
The investigating judge excepcianally may give a reasoned decision on incommunicado detention or imprisonment when any of the following circumstances concur:

a) urgent need to avoid serious consequences that could endanger the life, freedom or physical integrity of a person, or

b) urgent need for immediate action by the investigating judges to avoid seriously compromising the criminal procedure.

provisions.comment: This provision seems to contradict Article 8.1.c) of the Directive, while the communications of the detainee with her/his lawyer and third parties are limited considering exclusively the type of crime
provisions.textEn: In relation to a person detained for the reasons expressed in the previous paragraph (offense committed by a person integrated or related to armed gangs or terrorist groups or rebel individuals), the Judge may be requested to decree his/her incommunicado detention, which must be decided in reasoned resolution, within twenty-four hours. Upon request for incommunicado detention, the detainee shall remain incommunicado in any case without prejudice to the right of defense that assists him/her and the provisions of articles 520 and 527, until the Judge decides

items.text:
(d)

not prejudice the overall fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: According to this provision, the incommunicado detainee retains his/her right of defense and s/he must be informed of all his/her rights, except those that are expressly restricted, by reasoned decision, related to his communication with third parties. The lawyer assistance guarantees the overall fairness of the proceedings.
provisions.textEn: In relation to a person detained for the reasons expressed in the previous paragraph (offense committed by a person integrated or related to armed gangs or terrorist groups or rebel individuals), the Judge may be requested to decree his/her incommunicado detention, which must be decided in reasoned resolution, within twenty-four hours. items.text: 2. Temporary derogations under Article 3(5) or (6) may be authorised only by a duly reasoned decision taken on a case-by-case basis, either by a judicial authority, or by another competent authority on condition that the decision can be submitted to judicial review. The duly reasoned decision shall be recorded using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.

provisions.textEn: The lack of communication or restriction of another right of the previous section will be adopted by judicial order. When the restriction of rights is requested by the Judicial Police or by the Prosecutor's Office, the measures provided for in paragraph 1 shall be adopted for a maximum period of twenty-four hours, within which the judge shall decide on the request, as well as on the need to declare the secret of the investigation procedure. The lack of communication and the application to the detainee or prisoner of any of the exceptions referred to in the previous section will be adopted by court order, and the reasons that justify the adoption of each of the exceptions to the general regime must be motivated in accordance with the provisions of the article 509.

items.text: 3. Temporary derogations under Article 5(3) may be authorised only on a case-by-case basis, either by a judicial authority, or by another competent authority on condition that the decision can be submitted to judicial review.

items.comment: The possibility of restricting the right to have a third person informed is not foreseen in the Spanish legislation, only the possibility of restricting communications or access to the materials of the case is foreseen. In any case, the incommunicado detention must be decided by a judicial authority in a reasoned decision in the light of the particular circumstances of the case and based on taxative reasons.

items.heading: Article 9

items.text: 1. Without prejudice to national law requiring the mandatory presence or assistance of a lawyer, Member States shall ensure that, in relation to any waiver of a right referred to in Articles 3 and 10:

(a)

the suspect or accused person has been provided, orally or in writing, with clear and sufficient information in simple and understandable language about the content of the right concerned and the possible consequences of waiving it; and

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The detainee or prisoner may waive the mandatory assistance of a lawyer if his/her detention is for acts that can be classified exclusively as crimes against traffic safety, provided that clear and sufficient information has been provided in a simple and understandable language about the content of such right and the consequences of the resignation. The detainee may revoke his resignation at any time.

the waiver is given voluntarily and unequivocally.

items.heading: Article 10
items.subHeading: The right of access to a lawyer in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that a requested person has the right of access to a lawyer in the executing Member State upon arrest pursuant to the European arrest warrant.

nationalActs.title: Ley 23/2014, de 20 de noviembre, de reconocimiento mutuo de resoluciones penales en la Unión Europea
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union

provisions.textEn: The hearing of the detained person shall be held within a maximum period of seventy-two hours since s/he is brought to justice, with the assistance of the Prosecutor's Office, the detainee's lawyer and, where appropriate, an interpreter, and must be carried out in accordance with provided for the declaration of the detainee by the Criminal Procedure Law. Likewise, the right of defense and, where legally applicable, free legal assistance will be guaranteed.

items.text: 2. With regard to the content of the right of access to a lawyer in the executing Member State, requested persons shall have the following rights in that Member State:

(a)

the right of access to a lawyer in such time and in such a manner as to allow the requested persons to exercise their rights effectively and in any event without undue delay from deprivation of liberty;

nationalActs.title: Ley 23/2014, de 20 de noviembre, de reconocimiento mutuo de resoluciones penales en la Unión Europea
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union

provisions.comment: There is no express mention of the effectiveness of the right of defense or the need to recognize it without undue delay. However, this provision is fully implemented since the Article 51.1 of the Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union contains a general reference to the provisions governing the detention of any other defendant according to the Criminal Procedural Act, where this specific guarantee and others are provided
provisions.textEn: The hearing of the detained person shall be held within a maximum period of seventy-two hours since s/he is brought to justice, with the assistance of the Prosecutor's Office, the detainee's lawyer and, where appropriate, an interpreter, and must be carried out in accordance with provided for the declaration of the detainee by the Criminal Procedural Law. Likewise, the right of defense and, where legally applicable, free legal assistance will be guaranteed.

items.text:
(b)

the right to meet and communicate with the lawyer representing them;

the right for their lawyer to be present and, in accordance with procedures in national law, participate during a hearing of a requested person by the executing judicial authority. items.text: 3. The rights provided for in Articles 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, and, where a temporary derogation under Article 5(3) is applied, in Article 8, shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to European arrest warrant proceedings in the executing Member State.

provisions.comment:
There is no express mention of the confidentiality of attorney-client communication, the right to have a third person informed of the deprivation of liberty, the right to communicate, while deprived of liberty, with third persons, the right to communicate with consular authorities or the general conditions for applying temporary derogations of the previous rights, for the detainee under a European Arrest Warrant.


The only relevant provision is the Article 51.1 of the Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union which contains a general reference to the provisions governing the declaration of any other detainee according to the Criminal Procedural Law. But in this case, this general reference seems insufficient since some of the guarantees are not applicable to any defendant, but only to the detainee.

Likewise, the right of defense and, where legally applicable, free legal assistance will be guaranteed.

items.text: 4. The competent authority in the executing Member State shall, without undue delay after deprivation of liberty, inform requested persons that they have the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State. The role of that lawyer in the issuing Member State is to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State by providing that lawyer with information and advice with a view to the effective exercise of the rights of requested persons under Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA.

nationalActs.titleEn: Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union

provisions.comment: This modification occurred through Law 3/2018, of June 11, which modified the Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the EU, to regulate the European Investigation Order.
provisions.textEn: Once the detained person is brought to justice, s/he will be informed of the existence of the European arrest warrant, of its contents, of his/her right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State whose function will be to assist the lawyer in Spain providing him/her with information and advice, of the possibility of consenting irrevocably his/her surrender to the issuing State in the hearing before the judge, as well as of the rest of his/her rights. In the event in which the appointment of a lawyer in the issuing State is requested, the issuing competent authority will be informed immediately

items.text: 5. Where requested persons wish to exercise the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State and do not already have such a lawyer, the competent authority in the executing Member State shall promptly inform the competent authority in the issuing Member State. The competent authority of that Member State shall, without undue delay, provide the requested persons with information to facilitate them in appointing a lawyer there.

provisions.comment: The intervention of Spain as issuing State consited of informing the detainee who is in the executing Member State is not expressly regulated.
provisions.textEn: Once the detained person is brought to justice, s/he will be informed of the existence of the European arrest warran, of its contents, of his right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State whose function will be to assist the lawyer in Spain providing him/her with information and advice, of the possibility of consenting irrevocably his/her surrender to the issuing State in the hearing before the judge, as well as of the rest of his/her rights. In the event in which the appointment of a lawyer in the issuing State is requested, the issuing competent authority will be informed immediately.

items.text: 6. The right of a requested person to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State is without prejudice to the time-limits set out in Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA or the obligation on the executing judicial authority to decide, within those time-limits and the conditions defined under that Framework Decision, whether the person is to be surrendered.

items.heading: Article 12

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, as well as requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings, have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of the rights under this Directive.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: It is possible to lodge an appeal when the procedure or the judgment has incurred in breach of the rules and procedural guarantees, which will cause defenselessness, if a claim for rectification has been timely made. This claim will not be necessary if the alleged violation involves the violation of a constitutionally guaranteed fundamental right (sucha as the right to be assited by a lawyer).

items.comment: In addition to the possible appeal, the violation of fundamental rights sucha as the right of defence, allows a cassation appeal to be lodged before the Supreme Court for violation of a constitutional provision and also an application for amparo before the Constitutional Court would.

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to national rules and systems on the admissibility of evidence, Member States shall ensure that, in criminal proceedings, in the assessment of statements made by suspects or accused persons or of evidence obtained in breach of their right to a lawyer or in cases where a derogation to this right was authorised in accordance with Article 3(6), the rights of the defence and the fairness of the proceedings are respected.

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial

provisions.comment: The right to defence and to be assisted by a lawyer are fundamental rights according to the Article 24 (2) of the Spanish Constitution. In view of their consideration of fundamental rights, evidence obtained by violating them is null and void.
provisions.textEn: Evidence obtained, directly or indirectly, violating the fundamental rights or freedoms will not take effect
